data.question: Can the headless, detect, autonomy and acp facts of claude and kilo be read on this machine with read-only probes only?

chunk_findings.detail: The default headless autonomy profile is set to `scoped`, whose argv string uses `--permission-mode dontAsk --allowedTools mcp__ddflow`. The same change’s `[facts."autonomy.profiles"]` note explicitly says that the effect of that combination “was NOT run,” and the corresponding probe is listed under `[verified].unverified`. Therefore any headless Claude invocation that uses descriptor defaults will pass an unverified permission profile; if `dontAsk` with `--allowedTools mcp__ddflow` does not actually permit the ddflow MCP tools (or still causes a prompt/denial in `-p` mode), the run will fail or hang instead of producing the expected stream-json. A default headless configuration should not select a profile whose crucial permission behavior is marked unverified.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/harnesses/claude.toml:82

chunk_findings.detail: The fact is marked `s = "verified"`, but its recorded evidence does not verify a process name. `src` says `probe: which kilo; kilo --version -> 7.8.27`, and `probe` is only `kilo --version`; neither command observes a running process. If `kilo` is launched through a wrapper or interpreter, the OS process name can be something other than `kilo` (for example `node` or `bash`), while `which kilo` still succeeds. Then detection that matches `[detect].process_names = ["kilo"]` will miss a running kilo process even though the fact is presented as verified.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/harnesses/kilo.toml:[facts."detect.process_names"]

chunk_findings.detail: The descriptor’s `[headless]` section does not describe the full documented kilo headless argv. `argv` is only `["kilo", "run"]`, and the added fields cover `--format`, `--model`, `--variant`, `--session`, and `--auto`, but there is no field or argv entry for `--dir` or `--file`. The fact note for `headless.argv` itself says the lane passes `--dir <worktree>` and `--file <task file>` and that “the descriptor has no field for them.” A descriptor-only consumer that builds the command from `[headless]`—for example with worktree `/wt`, task file `task.md`, and prompt `say ok`—will produce a `kilo run ... say ok` command without `--dir /wt --file task.md`, so the agent can run in the wrong directory and without the task file, contrary to the stated acceptance that the descriptor carries the current `--dir`/`--file` argv.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/harnesses/kilo.toml:[headless]

chunk_findings.detail: `_headless` still grades unknown/unverified `[headless]` facts as `ok`. For any descriptor with `[headless] argv=["opencode", "run"]` and either no `[facts."headless.*"]` rows or a row such as `[facts."headless.argv"] s = "unverified"`, the function returns `{"status": "ok", ...}`: if rows are synthesized, `left` is populated but the status is still `ok`; if rows are explicit-only, it returns `0 read ..., 0 unverified` and also `ok`. The enclosing conformance check computes `ok = all(c["status"] == "ok" ...)`, so `ddflow harness test` still reports the agent as ok over unknown, contrary to the stated intent and the function’s own docstring.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driver_conformance.py:_headless

chunk_findings.detail: For the fixed input `cwd="/w"`, the `expect` argv is `["kilo", "run", "--model", "m1", "--session", "s1", "--auto", "--format", "json"]` and never renders `--dir /w`. The stated acceptance says Kilo's headless argv includes `--dir`; if the descriptor renders `--dir {cwd}`, this fixture makes the test fail, and if the descriptor omits it, the fixture approves a launch that does not pass the requested workspace to Kilo (it will inherit the driver cwd instead). Given input `cwd="/w"`, the snapshot should include `--dir`, `/w`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/harness/kilo/engines/argv.json:13

chunk_findings.detail: The guard intended to ensure verified facts name only read-only probes is implemented as a substring check for `" -p "` and `" run "` (with trailing spaces). A verified fact with `probe = "claude -p"` or `probe = "kilo run"` passes because neither string contains the required trailing-space substring. Those probes are headless agent invocations, not `--version`/`--help`, so the test can pass while the descriptor records a verified fact whose probe would start an agent, contradicting the stated invariant.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_claude_kilo_headless.py:test_a_verified_fact_names_the_probe_and_the_tool_version

chunk_findings.detail: The check for “ok over unknown” only inspects the first colon-separated segment of `chk["detail"]`. If `DC.run` returns a headless check like `{"status": "ok", "detail": "ok: unknown fact (1 read, 1 unverified)"}`, the test passes: the status is `ok`, the first segment is `ok`, and the detail contains both `read` and `unverified`. The unknown condition is still present in the detail and would be missed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_claude_kilo_headless.py:test_harness_test_grades_headless_not_ok_over_unknown

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert "--format" not in plan["kilo"] or "json" in plan["kilo"]` accepts any kilo plan command whose text contains `json` after `--format`, including `--format jsonl` or `--format json-lines`. For example, a plan command `kilo run --auto --format jsonl` passes the assertion even though the required kilo headless format is not exactly `json`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_claude_kilo_headless.py:test_the_agent_smoke_plan_lists_claude_and_kilo

chunk_findings.detail: The new reserved-section guard only exempts `claude` and `kilo` from `h.reserved == {}`; it never checks that their reserved content is actually just `[acp]`. For example, if `claude.toml` gains an unknown `[bogus]` section that the loader puts into `h.reserved`, the test still passes because `h.id not in ACP_DECLARED` is false, even though the comment says `[acp]` is “the one reserved section a shipped descriptor fills.” The intended guard against unverified reserved sections is therefore unenforced for the two allowed descriptors.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_descriptor_v2.py:44

chunk_findings.detail: The descriptor selects `output_format = "stream-json"` but never encodes `--verbose` or a version guard, while the same file admits that `stream-json` under `-p` may require `--verbose` and lists that as unverified (`[facts."headless.output_format"]` note and `[verified].unverified`). Because `[detect]` matches any `claude` process name with no version check, a machine still on an older 2.1.x build can be graded with this descriptor. The constructed command `claude -p --output-format stream-json ...` then fails or emits no usable stream before the model call, so headless grading is wrong.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/harnesses/claude.toml:[headless] output_format

chunk_findings.detail: The default headless profile is `autonomy = "scoped"`, but the only fact for that profile says the operative permission behavior was not run: `[facts."autonomy.profiles"]` marks the flags as read from help, and `[verified].unverified` explicitly lists the probe needed to show that `--permission-mode dontAsk --allowedTools mcp__ddflow` lets ddflow MCP tools run. A default headless claude run therefore relies on an unverified permission profile; if the allow rule does not match the actual MCP tool names or `dontAsk` denies, the child exits/blocks with a permission error instead of returning a result, so `ddflow harness test claude` should not grade this as a verified headless path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/harnesses/claude.toml:[headless] autonomy

chunk_findings.detail: The new headless grader never returns a non-`ok` status for unverified headless facts. For a descriptor with `[headless] argv = ["x"]` and `[facts."headless.argv"] s = "unverified"`, `rows` contains one headless fact, `read` is empty, `left` is `["headless.argv"]`, but the function still returns `{"status": "ok", ...}`. The caller then includes that check in `all(c["status"] == "ok")`, so the harness passes even though no headless fact is readable. This directly contradicts the change’s stated goal that headless should no longer be “ok over unknown” and the function’s own docstring, which says an unread headless section should “say so (`unverified`)”.
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/services/driver_conformance.py:_headless`

chunk_findings.detail: `argv_for` silently drops a requested autonomy profile when the descriptor names one but does not provide it. Given a descriptor with `[headless] argv = ["kilo", "run"]`, `output_flag = "--format"`, `output_format = "json"`, `model_flag = "--model"`, and `autonomy = "auto"`, but with `[autonomy.profiles]` missing or with `auto` misspelled, the `.get(head.autonomy, "").split()` fallback returns an empty tuple, so the generated command omits `--auto`. For kilo/opencode headless runs this can leave the CLI waiting for permission/input instead of running unattended. Since the function already raises a `ValueError` when `[headless].argv` is missing, a declared but unavailable autonomy profile should also fail loudly rather than produce a malformed headless command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/opencode.py:argv_for

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture is declared to be a snapshot of the rendered `[headless]` argv for fixed inputs, and `inputs.cwd` is `/w`, but the expected argv omits `--dir /w` even though the change’s acceptance criterion says kilo’s headless argv uses `--dir`. If the descriptor is corrected to pass the requested working directory via `--dir`, this fixture will fail; if the descriptor is left to match the fixture, `kilo run` is launched without the `--dir` flag the change claims to have recorded, so a non-default cwd is not passed to the binary.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/harness/kilo/engines/argv.json:13

chunk_findings.detail: The guard intended to keep verified fact probes read-only is bypassed by probes that end at the dangerous token. The assertion looks for `" -p "` and `" run "` with trailing spaces, so a verified fact whose probe is `probe = "claude -p"` or `probe = "kilo run"` passes the check even though both commands would start an agent run if used. This lets a descriptor record a probe that violates the change’s own rule that nothing beyond `--version`/`--help` is run.
chunk_findings.title: `test_a_verified_fact_names_the_probe_and_the_tool_version`

chunk_findings.detail: The test does not ensure each unverified fact has its own command; it only counts total occurrences of `probe:` in the joined text. For example, if `h.verified.unverified = ["exit codes and max-turns probe: claude --version probe: extra"]`, the test passes: the text contains `"exit codes"`, `"max-turns"`, and at least two `probe:` substrings, even though the `max-turns` fact has no exact command. The assertion message claims each such fact names the exact command, but the test accepts data that does not.
chunk_findings.title: `test_what_needs_a_model_run_is_listed_with_its_command`

chunk_findings.detail: The check that the headless grade is not “ok over unknown” only inspects the text before the first colon. If `DC.run` returns `{"checks": {"headless": {"status": "ok", "detail": "headless: ok over unknown (read 3, unverified 2)"}}}`, all assertions pass: status is `ok`, `"unknown"` is not in `"headless"`, and the detail contains `"read"` and `"unverified"`. Thus the test can accept an unknown-based grade as long as the word `unknown` appears after the first colon.
chunk_findings.title: `test_harness_test_grades_headless_not_ok_over_unknown`

chunk_findings.detail: The new guard skips the reserved-section assertion for every descriptor listed in `ACP_DECLARED`, so the test no longer enforces the stated invariant that `[acp]` is the only reserved section a shipped descriptor may fill. For example, if `ddflow/harnesses/claude.toml` contains `[reserved.acp]` plus an unrelated `[reserved.bogus]` table, or even only `[reserved.bogus]`, `h.reserved` will not be `{}`, but the test passes because `h.id == "claude"`. This can silently ship malformed or unintended reserved descriptor data and also allows `ACP_DECLARED` to claim acp facts for a descriptor that actually has no `[acp]` section.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_descriptor_v2.py:41

chunk_findings.detail: The new read-only probe guard accepts any probe whose first token is `env`. For example, a verified fact with `probe = "env claude -p hi"` (or `probe = "env kilo run"`) passes because `words[0] == "env"`, even though that probe would launch an agent rather than merely list the environment. This defeats the test’s stated purpose and the change’s acceptance that verified facts be backed by read-only probes only (`--version`, `--help`, or an environment listing). The check should accept only an actual environment listing, not any command beginning with `env`.

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert "--format" not in plan["kilo"] or "json" in plan["kilo"]` accepts any kilo plan command whose text contains `json` after `--format`, including `--format jsonl` or `--format json-lines`. For example, a plan command `kilo run --auto --format jsonl` passes the assertion even though the required kilo headless format is not exactly `json`.

chunk_findings.detail: The new reserved-section guard only exempts `claude` and `kilo` from `h.reserved == {}`; it never checks that their reserved content is actually just `[acp]`. For example, if `claude.toml` gains an unknown `[bogus]` section that the loader puts into `h.reserved`, the test still passes because `h.id not in ACP_DECLARED` is false, even though the comment says `[acp]` is “the one reserved section a shipped descriptor fills.” The intended guard against unverified reserved sections is therefore unenforced for the two allowed descriptors.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_descriptor_v2.py:44

chunk_findings.detail: The new note explicitly records that a running kilo process was seen by `ps` as `comm MainThread` with args `node $HOME/.local/bin/kilo`, and says “a match on the running process comm would miss it.” The delta only changes this note; the actual `detect.process_names` fact remains the old `kilo`-name fact, whose evidence is still `kilo --version`. Thus, given a running kilo, a detector that uses the recorded process name/comm to find it (e.g. `pgrep -x kilo` or equivalent) will not match `MainThread`/`node`, while the descriptor still presents the process-name fact as verified. The note confirms the mismatch instead of correcting the process-name fact or its status.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/harnesses/kilo.toml:92 `[facts."detect.process_names"]`

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_headless` logic returns `ok` whenever at least one headless fact is readable, even if other headless facts are unverified. For a descriptor with `[headless].argv` and fact rows such as `headless.argv` verified plus `headless.model` unverified, `read` is non-empty and `left` is non-empty, so `_headless` returns `{"status": "ok", "detail": "1 read ..., 1 unverified: headless.model"}`. The enclosing `conformance` call sees only `ok` statuses and returns `ok`, so `ddflow harness test` still grades a headless section as passing over unknown facts. The previous “ok over unknown” issue is only fixed for the zero-readable-facts case, not for mixed verified/unverified headless facts.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driver_conformance.py:104 `_headless`

chunk_findings.detail: The new read-only probe guard accepts any probe whose first token is `env`. For example, a verified fact with `probe = "env claude -p hi"` (or `probe = "env kilo run"`) passes because `words[0] == "env"`, even though that probe would launch an agent rather than merely list the environment. This defeats the test’s stated purpose and the change’s acceptance that verified facts be backed by read-only probes only (`--version`, `--help`, or an environment listing). The check should accept only an actual environment listing, not any command beginning with `env`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_claude_kilo_headless.py:test_a_verified_fact_names_the_probe_and_the_tool_version

chunk_findings.detail: The new read-only probe guard treats any probe string beginning with `env | grep ^` as safe, so a compound shell command can pass even though it launches an agent. For example, a fact row with `probe = "env | grep ^DDFLOW_ && claude -p hi"` makes `env_listing` true and the assertion succeeds, despite the probe not being “the one environment listing piped to grep” and not being read-only. The same applies to `env | grep ^PATH; kilo run` or `env | grep ^PATH\nclaude -p hi`. This defeats the stated purpose of the guard: verified facts are supposed to be backed only by `--version`, `--help`, or a pure environment listing.

chunk_findings.detail: The descriptor selects `output_format = "stream-json"` but never encodes `--verbose` or a version guard, while the same file admits that `stream-json` under `-p` may require `--verbose` and lists that as unverified (`[facts."headless.output_format"]` note and `[verified].unverified`). Because `[detect]` matches any `claude` process name with no version check, a machine still on an older 2.1.x build can be graded with this descriptor. The constructed command `claude -p --output-format stream-json ...` then fails or emits no usable stream before the model call, so headless grading is wrong.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/harnesses/claude.toml:[headless] output_format

chunk_findings.detail: The default headless profile is `autonomy = "scoped"`, but the only fact for that profile says the operative permission behavior was not run: `[facts."autonomy.profiles"]` marks the flags as read from help, and `[verified].unverified` explicitly lists the probe needed to show that `--permission-mode dontAsk --allowedTools mcp__ddflow` lets ddflow MCP tools run. A default headless claude run therefore relies on an unverified permission profile; if the allow rule does not match the actual MCP tool names or `dontAsk` denies, the child exits/blocks with a permission error instead of returning a result, so `ddflow harness test claude` should not grade this as a verified headless path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/harnesses/claude.toml:[headless] autonomy

chunk_findings.detail: The new headless grader never returns a non-`ok` status for unverified headless facts. For a descriptor with `[headless] argv = ["x"]` and `[facts."headless.argv"] s = "unverified"`, `rows` contains one headless fact, `read` is empty, `left` is `["headless.argv"]`, but the function still returns `{"status": "ok", ...}`. The caller then includes that check in `all(c["status"] == "ok")`, so the harness passes even though no headless fact is readable. This directly contradicts the change’s stated goal that headless should no longer be “ok over unknown” and the function’s own docstring, which says an unread headless section should “say so (`unverified`)”.
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/services/driver_conformance.py:_headless`

chunk_findings.detail: `argv_for` silently drops a requested autonomy profile when the descriptor names one but does not provide it. Given a descriptor with `[headless] argv = ["kilo", "run"]`, `output_flag = "--format"`, `output_format = "json"`, `model_flag = "--model"`, and `autonomy = "auto"`, but with `[autonomy.profiles]` missing or with `auto` misspelled, the `.get(head.autonomy, "").split()` fallback returns an empty tuple, so the generated command omits `--auto`. For kilo/opencode headless runs this can leave the CLI waiting for permission/input instead of running unattended. Since the function already raises a `ValueError` when `[headless].argv` is missing, a declared but unavailable autonomy profile should also fail loudly rather than produce a malformed headless command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/opencode.py:argv_for

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture is declared to be a snapshot of the rendered `[headless]` argv for fixed inputs, and `inputs.cwd` is `/w`, but the expected argv omits `--dir /w` even though the change’s acceptance criterion says kilo’s headless argv uses `--dir`. If the descriptor is corrected to pass the requested working directory via `--dir`, this fixture will fail; if the descriptor is left to match the fixture, `kilo run` is launched without the `--dir` flag the change claims to have recorded, so a non-default cwd is not passed to the binary.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/harness/kilo/engines/argv.json:13

chunk_findings.detail: The guard intended to keep verified fact probes read-only is bypassed by probes that end at the dangerous token. The assertion looks for `" -p "` and `" run "` with trailing spaces, so a verified fact whose probe is `probe = "claude -p"` or `probe = "kilo run"` passes the check even though both commands would start an agent run if used. This lets a descriptor record a probe that violates the change’s own rule that nothing beyond `--version`/`--help` is run.
chunk_findings.title: `test_a_verified_fact_names_the_probe_and_the_tool_version`

chunk_findings.detail: The test does not ensure each unverified fact has its own command; it only counts total occurrences of `probe:` in the joined text. For example, if `h.verified.unverified = ["exit codes and max-turns probe: claude --version probe: extra"]`, the test passes: the text contains `"exit codes"`, `"max-turns"`, and at least two `probe:` substrings, even though the `max-turns` fact has no exact command. The assertion message claims each such fact names the exact command, but the test accepts data that does not.
chunk_findings.title: `test_what_needs_a_model_run_is_listed_with_its_command`

chunk_findings.detail: The check that the headless grade is not “ok over unknown” only inspects the text before the first colon. If `DC.run` returns `{"checks": {"headless": {"status": "ok", "detail": "headless: ok over unknown (read 3, unverified 2)"}}}`, all assertions pass: status is `ok`, `"unknown"` is not in `"headless"`, and the detail contains `"read"` and `"unverified"`. Thus the test can accept an unknown-based grade as long as the word `unknown` appears after the first colon.
chunk_findings.title: `test_harness_test_grades_headless_not_ok_over_unknown`

chunk_findings.detail: The new guard skips the reserved-section assertion for every descriptor listed in `ACP_DECLARED`, so the test no longer enforces the stated invariant that `[acp]` is the only reserved section a shipped descriptor may fill. For example, if `ddflow/harnesses/claude.toml` contains `[reserved.acp]` plus an unrelated `[reserved.bogus]` table, or even only `[reserved.bogus]`, `h.reserved` will not be `{}`, but the test passes because `h.id == "claude"`. This can silently ship malformed or unintended reserved descriptor data and also allows `ACP_DECLARED` to claim acp facts for a descriptor that actually has no `[acp]` section.

That contradicts the change’s invariant that verified fact probes are read-only (`--version`/`--help`) and would allow a descriptor to record a probe that starts an agent run.

chunk_findings.detail: The new read-only probe guard still accepts any recorded probe that merely starts with `env | grep ^`, not only a complete environment listing. For example, a fact row can set `probe = "env | grep ^PATH && kilo run"`; `env_listing` becomes true, so the assertion passes even though the recorded probe would start an agent run rather than perform a read-only `--version`/`--help` probe. This contradicts the change’s invariant that verified fact probes are read-only and leaves a variant of the previous `env` bypass open.
